title: Dimethylglycine in WWOX-LoF
summary: A comparison of local mitochondrial substrate use and peripheral conversion.

graph.evidence: DMGDH transcript is scarce in three WWOX bulk models and two pooled nuclear matrices.
graph.inference: Local conversion and productive electron transfer remain separate questions.
graph.hypothesis: A substrate deficit could matter only in cells with retained DMGDH and ETF activity.
graph.experiment: Pair labeled product with ATP recovery under matched neural workload.

evidence: DMGDH stayed below 1 on the deposited scale in both arms of all three WWOX bulk comparisons. The CSF meal result reproduced at 2.16-fold from three paired observations, with 1.03-fold in plasma.
inference: A blood increase in a five-child mitochondrial crossover accompanied no demonstrated gain in whole-body oxygen consumption. The printed blood concentration unit remains unresolved.
hypothesis: Peripheral production of downstream metabolites could mimic a response to the parent. Local product could also form without an ATP gain.
experiment: Track methyl label into sarcosine and a one-carbon product together with ATP recovery and evoked recruitment. Compare local DMGDH interruption and matched sarcosine or glycine.
limits: Retain as a conditional tracer and defer pediatric WWOX priority. Free neural exposure, local enzyme activity and functional benefit remain unmeasured.
